- **Status:** alive  <sub>[v5 c5 P128](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0128), [v5 c33 P22](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0022)</sub>
- **Role:** minister  <sub>[v5 c9 P88](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0088), [v5 c33 P22](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0022)</sub>
- **Titles:** recluse of Glen St. Mary manse  <sub>[v5 c13 P10](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0010)</sub>; the Glen minister  <sub>[v5 c9 P88](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0088), [v5 c32 P47](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0047)</sub>

## Appearance

In his youth, he went by the name Jack and had the heart of a boy. When deep in theological study, he has been seen with unbrushed hair, dressed in carpet slippers and a faded dressing gown.

_Sources: [v5 c13 P2](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0002), [v5 c14 P0](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0000)_

## Personality

John Meredith is shy, aloof, and extremely absent-minded, often becoming so absorbed in theological studies that he forgets meals, church meetings, and his surroundings. Beneath his quiet exterior he possesses the heart of a boy and deep, sensitive feelings. He is a deeply caring father who loves his children profoundly, though his intense scholarly absorption often leaves him unmindful of practical everyday affairs. He is also easily mortified and intimidated by sharp or overbearing people.

_Sources: [v5 c5 P128](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0128), [v5 c9 P86](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0086), [v5 c13 P2](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0002), [v5 c14 P0](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0000), [v5 c14 P36](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0036), [v5 c14 P37](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0037), [v5 c21 P3](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0003), [v5 c22 P41](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0041)_

## History

John Meredith served as the minister of Glen St. Mary while raising his four motherless children—Jerry, Faith, Una, and Carl—at the manse. Constantly absorbed in theological reading and sermon preparations, he frequently lost track of time, forgetting meals, pastoral visits, and even parish meetings. After a harsh confrontation from Mrs. Alec Davis regarding his neglect of his children's upbringing, John was deeply shaken and sought counsel from Mrs. Blythe, realizing his personal shortcomings as a father. Around the same time, he struck up a close friendship with Walter Blythe and encountered Rosemary West at a spring in Rainbow Valley. Realizing he had fallen deeply in love with Rosemary, he eventually asked her to marry him, but received a stiff, written refusal that left him heartbroken. Despite his grief, he resolved to take up his duties alone and try to be a more attentive father to his children.

_Sources: [v5 c5 P128](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0128), [v5 c9 P85](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0085), [v5 c9 P86](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0086), [v5 c9 P88](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0088), [v5 c13 P2](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0002), [v5 c13 P5](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0005), [v5 c14 P0](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0000), [v5 c14 P36](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0036), [v5 c14 P37](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0037), [v5 c21 P0](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0000), [v5 c21 P1](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0001), [v5 c22 P41](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0041), [v5 c28 P26](../source/v05-c28.md#nw-v05-c28-p0026)_
